narrative:
The model estimates an 80% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system has learned from many similar employee profiles.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outlook were your overall years of experience, the time you have spent in your current role, and whether you have received other job offers. 

Your 6–10 years of total experience pushed the prediction toward leaving. While many employees predicted to stay have shorter careers (1–5 years is most common among stayers), the model sees your mid-level experience as a point where people often begin exploring new opportunities. Similarly, having spent 1–5 years in this organization also contributed to the “will leave” direction; this tenure is typical among those who eventually move on rather than settle long-term.

Receiving other job opportunities was the third strongest influence and further increased the likelihood of departure. The combination of these three elements created a clear signal that you are at a stage where changing employers becomes more probable.

The organization should consider discussing your career goals with you openly and exploring whether additional responsibilities, clearer growth paths, or improved work-life support could increase your commitment. You may also want to reflect on what would make staying more attractive before making any decisions. (218 words)
